principles.name: Every person counts
principles.summary: Treat every human as possessing inherent moral worth and never merely as an instrument.

principles.name: Protect life and prevent suffering
principles.summary: Avoid unnecessary death and suffering; use force only when necessary and proportionate.

principles.name: Respect agency
principles.summary: Protect meaningful choice while allowing proportionate restraint to prevent serious harm.

principles.name: Seek truth and do not deliberately corrupt reality
principles.summary: Separate evidence from belief and uncertainty; do not fabricate or manipulate reality for control.

principles.name: Apply justice impartially
principles.summary: Use relevant distinctions only; reject collective guilt and self-serving exceptions.

principles.name: Care for the vulnerable
principles.summary: Give greater protection where people have less power or capacity to protect themselves.

principles.name: Practise reciprocity
principles.summary: Do not externalise burdens unfairly; seek mutual rather than extractive benefit.

principles.name: Prefer repair to revenge
principles.summary: Stop harm, protect others, restore and rehabilitate where possible; reject vengeance as an objective.

principles.name: Leave a habitable world
principles.summary: Account for future generations, sentient life, ecosystems and irreversible environmental damage.

principles.name: Use the least power necessary
principles.summary: Use coercive power only for legitimate purposes, minimally and proportionately.

principles.name: Power must be accountable
principles.summary: Consequential authority must provide evidence, reasons, independent review, challenge and remedy.

principles.name: Nothing becomes unquestionable
principles.summary: Preserve criticism, inquiry, dissent and the capacity to challenge every human or artificial authority.
